name: Desktop

# Builds Moneo Desktop on Windows, macOS and Linux, smoke-tests the packaged app, and on a `v*` tag
# drafts a GitHub release with the installers. Packages are unsigned unless the signing secrets exist.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "desktop/**"
      - "scripts/desktop/**"
      - "next.config.ts"
      - "package*.json"
      - "supabase/migrations/**"
      - ".github/workflows/desktop.yml"
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: desktop-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  build:
    name: ${{ matrix.id }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 60
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - { id: win-x64, runner: windows-latest, builder: "--win --x64" }
          - { id: mac-arm64, runner: macos-15, builder: "--mac --arm64" }
          # macos-13 was retired; macos-15-intel is the remaining Intel runner, so mac-x64 builds
          # and is smoke-tested natively.
          - { id: mac-x64, runner: macos-15-intel, builder: "--mac --x64" }
          - { id: linux-x64, runner: ubuntu-24.04, builder: "--linux --x64" }
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm

      # No setup-go: fetch-backend.mjs downloads its own pinned Go toolchain into desktop/.cache.
      - run: npm ci

      - uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: desktop/.cache
          key: desktop-cache-${{ matrix.id }}-${{ hashFiles('scripts/desktop/fetch-backend.mjs') }}

      - name: Fetch the native backend
        run: node scripts/desktop/fetch-backend.mjs --platform ${{ matrix.id }}

      - run: npm run desktop:build

      - name: Package
        env:
          CSC_LINK: ${{ secrets.CSC_LINK }}
          CSC_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.CSC_KEY_PASSWORD }}
          APPLE_ID: ${{ secrets.APPLE_ID }}
          APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD }}
          APPLE_TEAM_ID: ${{ secrets.APPLE_TEAM_ID }}
          WIN_CSC_LINK: ${{ secrets.WIN_CSC_LINK }}
          WIN_CSC_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.WIN_CSC_KEY_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          # Secrets that do not exist arrive as empty strings; unset them so electron-builder
          # treats the build as unsigned.
          for name in CSC_LINK CSC_KEY_PASSWORD APPLE_ID APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD APPLE_TEAM_ID WIN_CSC_LINK WIN_CSC_KEY_PASSWORD; do
            if [ -z "${!name}" ]; then unset "$name"; fi
          done
          if [ -z "${CSC_LINK:-}" ] && [ -z "${WIN_CSC_LINK:-}" ]; then
            export CSC_IDENTITY_AUTO_DISCOVERY=false
            echo "No signing certificate: building unsigned packages."
          fi
          npm run desktop:dist -- ${{ matrix.builder }} --publish never
          # Both Mac jobs write latest-mac.yml. Macs only read the version from it (unsigned apps
          # download from the release page), so the Apple Silicon one is kept.
          if [ "${{ matrix.id }}" = "mac-x64" ]; then rm -f desktop/release/latest-mac.yml; fi

      - name: List packages
        run: ls -la desktop/release

      # The smoke test starts the unpacked app (own temporary home, no cloud calls).
      - name: Linux dependencies for the smoke test
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y xvfb libnss3-tools
          # Ubuntu 24.04 blocks the unprivileged user namespaces Chromium's sandbox needs.
          sudo sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0

      - name: Smoke test
        run: |
          mkdir -p smoke
          if [ "$RUNNER_OS" = "Linux" ]; then
            xvfb-run -a --server-args="-screen 0 1280x1024x24" npm run desktop:smoke 2>&1 | tee "smoke/smoke-${{ matrix.id }}.log"
          else
            npm run desktop:smoke 2>&1 | tee "smoke/smoke-${{ matrix.id }}.log"
          fi

      - name: Upload installers
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: moneo-desktop-${{ matrix.id }}
          path: |
            desktop/release/*.exe
            desktop/release/*.dmg
            desktop/release/*.zip
            desktop/release/*.AppImage
            desktop/release/*.deb
            desktop/release/*.blockmap
            desktop/release/latest*.yml
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 7

      - name: Upload smoke logs
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: smoke-${{ matrix.id }}
          path: smoke/
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 3

  release:
    name: Draft release
    if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          pattern: moneo-desktop-*
          path: installers
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: Draft the release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          version=$(node -p "require('./desktop/package.json').version")
          if [ "$TAG" != "v$version" ]; then
            echo "::warning::Tag $TAG does not match desktop/package.json version $version; installer file names carry $version."
          fi
          cd installers
          ls -la
          files=$(find . -maxdepth 1 -type f \( -name '*.exe' -o -name '*.dmg' -o -name '*.zip' -o -name '*.AppImage' -o -name '*.deb' -o -name '*.blockmap' -o -name 'latest*.yml' \) -printf '%f\n' | sort)
          if [ -z "$files" ]; then echo "::error::No installers were downloaded."; exit 1; fi
          # shellcheck disable=SC2086
          sha256sum $files > SHA256SUMS.txt
          cat SHA256SUMS.txt
          # shellcheck disable=SC2086
          gh release create "$TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --draft --verify-tag \
            --title "Moneo Desktop $TAG" \
            --notes "Moneo Desktop $TAG. Packages are unsigned unless noted; check SHA256SUMS.txt." \
            $files SHA256SUMS.txt

result.output:
# Moneo

Moneo is an open-source personal finance app that runs on your own computer. Import bank statements or sync your bank, track accounts and wealth, plan spending, and ask questions about your money in chat or on a voice call. Figures always come from your own records; the AI explains them and suggests changes that you accept.

Everything stays on your computer. There are no accounts and no sign-in screen: one owner, one workspace. The only data that leaves your computer goes to the services you connect (your AI provider, and optionally your bank or Scalable Capital).

## Install

### Desktop preview

Desktop installers for Windows, macOS and Linux are attached to [GitHub releases](https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/releases) once published: download, install and open Moneo; nothing else is needed. Settings → App updates installs newer releases and keeps your data. See [desktop setup and operation](desktop/README.md) for packaging, data locations, backups and signing requirements. The desktop app bundles its local backend and does not require Docker or Node.js. The source installation below remains supported.
Scalable questions in chat and voice can combine live holdings, paginated transaction history and transaction details with local JavaScript calculations. The calculation sandbox has no network, filesystem or credentials. Read results remain subject to your AI data scopes and are sent to your configured AI provider as needed to answer. Trades still require accepting an approval card. No additional setup is needed.

### Easiest: let an AI agent install it

If you use an AI coding agent such as Claude Code or Codex, it can do the install for you with the `moneo-setup` skill that comes with Moneo. Open the agent in an empty folder and paste:

> Clone https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo, then set it up by following .agents/skills/moneo-setup/SKILL.md in that repository.

If you already downloaded Moneo, open the agent in the Moneo folder and say **"set up Moneo"**. The agent runs the commands, tells you what each step does, and asks you only for what it can't do itself, like installing Docker or entering your keys in Moneo. If it can control your browser or computer, it asks first and then does the clicking too. You type passwords and keys yourself.
  then the app window opens Home. On failure it offers Try again, Open logs folder, Restore from backup, Quit.
- Closing the window keeps Moneo in the tray, so background syncs and phone access keep working.
  Quit (tray, Cmd+Q, `Moneo --quit`, OS shutdown) stops the server, then the database, then exits.
- Daily automatic backup while running; Back up now, Open backups folder and Restore from backup in the tray.
- Sign-ins (ChatGPT, banks, Scalable) open in the system browser and return to Moneo's loopback
  callbacks. The callback then opens its result (Import or Settings) in the app window and brings it
  to the front; the browser tab says to continue in Moneo. The server reaches the window through a
  loopback address that is random for each launch and refuses browser requests (`src/bridge.ts`);
  if the window cannot take it, the browser shows the result as in a source checkout. Every other address also goes to the browser
  (https only). The window allows only the microphone and copying, for Moneo's own pages.
- Updates: Settings → App updates checks the newest published GitHub release only when the owner
  asks (`src/updates.ts`, electron-updater). On Windows and with the AppImage, Update downloads it,
  quits Moneo cleanly, installs it and starts Moneo again; data stays in the user folder, and a pending
  migration makes a `pre-upgrade` backup first. macOS (unsigned) and `.deb` installs open the release
  page to download instead. Draft and pre-releases are never offered. `npm run desktop:dist` writes
  the `latest*.yml` files the check reads; the release workflow uploads them with the installers.

## Releasing

Push a `v*` tag matching `desktop/package.json`'s version (bump it first). The Desktop workflow builds
every platform and drafts a release with the installers, `latest*.yml`, blockmaps and `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
Publish the draft on GitHub; from then on, Settings → App updates offers it to installed apps.

### Bank return certificate

Enable Banking returns to `https://localhost:3443`. On every start Moneo makes that certificate with the
bundled mkcert if it is missing (its signing authority lives in the user folder, `mkcert/`); nothing is
trusted yet. The first time the owner opens a bank's consent page, Moneo explains why and asks the
computer to trust that authority once: Windows shows its own confirmation (current user's store),
macOS asks for the login keychain password, Linux adds it to the browsers' NSS store (needs `certutil`).
